## Proof

**Claim.** For any positive integers $n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_c$ and any permutation $\sigma \in S_c$,
$$R(n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_c) = R(n_{\sigma(1)}, n_{\sigma(2)}, \ldots, n_{\sigma(c)}).$$

**Definition.** $R(n_1, \ldots, n_c)$ is the least integer $N$ such that every $c$-colouring of the edges of the complete graph $K_N$ (with colours $\{1, \ldots, c\}$) admits, for some $i \in \{1,\ldots,c\}$, a monochromatic copy of $K_{n_i}$ all of whose edges receive colour $i$.

**Proof.** Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{1,\ldots,c\}$ and set $p_i = n_{\sigma(i)}$. We show $R(n_1,\ldots,n_c) = R(p_1,\ldots,p_c)$.

Let $N = R(n_1,\ldots,n_c)$. We prove $N \geq R(p_1,\ldots,p_c)$; the reverse inequality follows by symmetry (applying $\sigma^{-1}$).

Take any $c$-colouring $\chi : E(K_N) \to \{1,\ldots,c\}$. Define a new colouring $\chi' = \sigma^{-1} \circ \chi$, i.e., relabel each colour $j$ by $\sigma^{-1}(j)$. Since $N = R(n_1,\ldots,n_c)$, the colouring $\chi'$ contains, for some index $i$, a monochromatic $K_{n_i}$ in colour $i$ under $\chi'$.

Under the original colouring $\chi$, this same set of vertices has all its edges coloured $\sigma(i)$ (since $\chi = \sigma \circ \chi'$). Thus $\chi$ contains a monochromatic $K_{n_i}$ in colour $\sigma(i)$. Setting $j = \sigma(i)$, this is a monochromatic $K_{n_{\sigma^{-1}(j)}} = K_{p_j}$ in colour $j$.

Therefore every $c$-colouring of $K_N$ contains a monochromatic $K_{p_j}$ in colour $j$ for some $j$, which means $N \geq R(p_1,\ldots,p_c)$.

By the identical argument with $\sigma^{-1}$, we obtain $R(p_1,\ldots,p_c) \geq R(n_1,\ldots,n_c)$. Hence the two numbers are equal. $\blacksquare$

**Remark.** The key insight is that the quantifier in the definition of Ramsey numbers ranges over *all* $c$-colourings. Permuting the colour labels is a bijection on the set of all $c$-colourings, so it preserves the universal quantifier. The sizes $n_i$ are simply re-paired with the colour labels by the same permutation, which is exactly what permuting the arguments accomplishes.

### PROOF COMPLETE
